subject: Azure Marketplace private plan — commercial split & co-sell entitlements
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@microsoft.com>, Procurement (Contoso) <procurement@contoso.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Azure private plan commercial & co-sell entitlements

Tara / Contoso procurement — thanks for taking the time last week. Per our call, attached is Redwood’s updated term sheet for an Azure Private Plan listing and the proposed commercial split for co-sell-qualified transactions. High-level summary: 

- Offer type: Azure Private Plan (non-transactable via marketplace cart; procurement via Contoso PO / Azure Marketplace private offer flow)
- List price (MSRP): $120,000 annual
- Proposed Azure marketplace commercial split for co-sell sales: 80/20 (Redwood / Contoso) for transactable offers; for private-plan purchases procured via Contoso PO we propose: 70/30 revenue split to Contoso after marketplace fee reconciliation
- Billing & invoicing: Redwood invoices Contoso monthly net-30; Azure handles marketplace compensation reconciliations per offer agreement
- Co-sell entitlement: Redwood requests joint-sell badges and eligibility for MS Co-sell incentives once offer appears in private listing (contingent on final offer registration)
- Data residency & audit: Redwood commits to customer-region residency for logs; SOC2 evidence can be provided on request

Questions we still have for procurement: how does Contoso prefer the legal signature flow (DocuSign or PO + countersign)? Also please confirm Contoso’s standard indemnity cap language; we included a mutual indemnity with a carveout for third-party IP in the attached term sheet.

Next steps I suggest: Contoso to provide a single consolidated redline to the attached term sheet by 8/13; Redwood legal (Laura) will review and, if small, we’ll push final to DocuSign and loop in Azure (Tara) to register the private plan. 

Attachments: Redwood_Azure_PrivatePlan_TermSheet_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119

From: Procurement (Contoso) <procurement@contoso.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@microsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Azure private plan commercial & co-sell entitlements

Soojin — thanks for the term sheet and the clear summary. A few items from procurement that need clarification before we send a formal redline: 

1) Revenue split wording: we need explicit language that defines "net distributable revenue" (i.e., after marketplace fees and tax withholding). Our finance team will require a 30-day reconciliation window after invoicing.
2) Billing flow: Contoso prefers to be invoiced via Azure marketplace charges when possible. If Redwood will invoice Contoso directly, we need a clause that allows Contoso to request supporting detail for line items within 45 days.
3) PO & signature: Contoso’s standard is to issue a PO and then countersign the supplier agreement. We do not use DocuSign for supplier agreements except in limited circumstances. Please confirm Redwood can accept PO + countersignature.
4) Liability cap: Contoso will request mutual cap at either 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months or $2M minimum; please advise position.

Please find initial SOW draft attached for commercial context (Contoso_SOW_draft.docx). We will circulate a full redline by 8/13 if the points above are addressable.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Contoso Inc.
procurement@contoso.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Procurement (Contoso) <procurement@contoso.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@microsoft.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Azure private plan commercial & co-sell entitlements

Thanks — quick responses inline to help unblock your procurement and finance teams: 

- \"Net distributable revenue\": we define this as gross paid to Redwood by Contoso via the Azure private offer process less Azure marketplace transaction fees and any taxes withheld. We can add an explicit reconciliation section with a 30-day window as requested.
- Billing flow: Redwood’s preference is marketplace billing where available for clearance and incentive tracking. If Contoso requires Redwood invoicing directly, Redwood will provide an itemized invoice and supporting detail within 10 business days of request (we can extend to 45 days to match your policy).
- PO + countersign: Redwood can accept PO + countersignature. We typically execute via DocuSign for speed, but we will accept your PO flow for this engagement.
- Liability cap: Redwood legal’s standard is 3x fees paid in prior 12 months; however, we can take $2M where the annual contract value is under $500K. For an ARR at the proposed MSRP, we need to discuss a hybrid cap; I’ve asked Laura (cc’d) to propose language that is acceptable.

Attached is v3 with the reconciliation and billing note added — Laura, can you confirm whether the liability language below is acceptable and whether the IP carveouts are satisfactory?

Action items:
- Contoso: please circulate consolidated redline by 8/13 (per your note)
- Laura: review liability/IP carveouts and advise by 8/14
- Tara/ Azure: once redline is agreed, please advise next steps to register the private plan and enable co-sell designation

Best,
Soojin

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Procurement (Contoso) <procurement@contoso.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@microsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Azure private plan commercial & co-sell entitlements

Soojin / team — I reviewed the v3 term sheet and Contoso’s SOW. High level: we can accept the majority of the changes proposed but recommend the following legal edits to be captured in the consolidated redline before signature: 

1) Liability cap: Agree to Redwood’s 3x fees approach for larger engagements; for clarity we propose the contract state: \"Cap equals the greater of (i) three times amounts paid by Contoso to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (ii) $2,000,000.\"
2) IP indemnity: keep mutual indemnity but add explicit customer-use clause; exclude open-source components per existing Redwood policy.
3) Payment disputes: add a 60-day cure period with an arbitration step for unresolved disputes to avoid contract termination for short-term disputes.
4) Co-sell badge: require Azure assistance to register the private plan for co-sell eligibility; Tara, please confirm that registration can proceed with the private plan doc once we complete the consolidated redline.

Assuming Contoso’s consolidated redline does not materially change the commercial split mechanics, I’m comfortable with PO+countersignature and the proposed reconciliation language. Marissa — please confirm whether accounting is ok to reconcile marketplace vs. direct invoicing with a 30-day window once the PO path is confirmed.

If Contoso returns a standard redline, we’ll aim to resolve comments and prepare an exec-approved contract for signature by 8/20.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
